title: Straining to urinate (especially a male cat)
signs: Repeated trips to the litter tray with little or no urine, crying, licking the genitals, hiding.
action: Emergency: see a vet immediately. Being unable to pass urine is a recognised emergency in cats.

title: Stops eating: contact your vet promptly
signs: Refuses all food. Kittens and overweight cats are at higher risk.
action: Contact your vet when you notice loss of appetite. Even 24 hours without food can seriously affect an adult cat. Kittens and ill cats need advice sooner. Not eating can cause serious illness, including hepatic lipidosis. Do not force food into the cat without vet advice.

title: Breathing with an open mouth, or laboured breathing
signs: Breathing with an open mouth, laboured or gasping breathing, belly heaving, or pale, blue or grey gums. Do not wait to see if it settles.
action: Emergency: keep the cat calm and cool, don't restrain it, call ahead and go to a vet or emergency clinic now.

title: Lily exposure
signs: Possible exposure to true lilies (Lilium) or daylilies (Hemerocallis): leaves, petals, pollen on fur, or vase water, even without symptoms. For an unidentified plant called a lily, send your vet a photograph or label.
action: Emergency: go to a vet immediately. Lilies can cause acute kidney failure within a few days; early treatment improves the chance of survival.

title: Dog flea or tick product containing permethrin
signs: Any suspected exposure, including close contact with a recently treated dog. Tremors, twitching, drooling or seizures can follow. Do not wait for symptoms.
action: Emergency: contact a vet or the Animal Poisons Helpline now. Never use dog spot-on products on cats.

title: Paralysis tick signs (east coast)
signs: Weak or wobbly legs, changed meow, retching, coughing, vomiting or breathing trouble. Finding a tick or a tick crater also needs immediate veterinary advice.
action: Emergency: see a vet at once, even if you cannot find a tick. Do not offer food or water or give anything orally when paralysis is suspected.

title: Swallowed a human medicine or toxin
signs: Paracetamol or ibuprofen (cats are especially sensitive to paracetamol), antifreeze, rat bait, or chewed unknown plants.
action: Emergency: call a vet or the Animal Poisons Helpline immediately. Do not induce vomiting unless a vet tells you to.

title: Sudden weakness or pain in the back legs
signs: Sudden loss of use of one or both back legs, crying out, signs of pain. Can be a blood clot (aortic thromboembolism), often a complication of heart disease.
action: Emergency: contact your vet immediately and be ready to go now.
